# Cost-down list (generated by `python -m rnd.bom`; prices are list / ESTIMATE, nothing bought)

**Robot BOM $6,713 landed** ($5,837 of lines + 15% contingency), **$6,888 with D20** (GIM8108-8 at pitch + elbow, +$175). Limit $5,500, aim $4,000 (R8); owner decision D26: cost-down redesign first. Gap: +$1,213 (+$1,388 with D20) to the limit, +$2,713 to the aim. Line detail: [BOM_v4.md](BOM_v4.md).

- The two arms are 46% of the robot; actuators alone (arms + base + lift + head) are 31%. D20 adds +$175 to the arm actuators.
- The inline-arm study ([inline_study.md](inline_study.md)) settles the direction: a D26 belt stage is ≈ $60–70 of parts, and every inline swap costs $45–380 more per joint (all-inline +$585–1,068 landed over B1; B1y's inline yaw +$100). There is no cost-down in more inline motors; the only inline joint, the roll, is the largest single owner trade below.
- Competitors ([competitors.md](competitors.md)): XLeRobot reaches ≈ $660 with STS3215 servos and one-handed payloads; Pip's money is in the 20 lb two-handed carry (R2c / R2d) and the safety chain, which the gates keep.

## Top 10 savings

Ranked by landed saving. Row 1 is the queued belt-roll idea: it is the only large one and it is **not** gate-neutral (flagged); rows 2–10 keep R2 strength, R17 pinch, A10 tip and the thermal rows passing (each with the checks it needs before it lands).

**Rows 2–10 together: −$736 landed → $5,976 (+$476 against the $5,500 limit; $6,151 with D20, +$651).** With row 1 as well: $5,413 (−$87; with D20 $5,588, +$88). The gate-neutral list does not reach $5,500 on its own: the rest is an owner trade (the belt roll, D20's scope, or the D9 sensor pack), not an engineering saving.

## Considered and not recommended

| Idea | Saving | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| All-inline arm (I1 / I2a / I2b) | −(+$585…1,068) | costs more, misses A10 or the hug at 0.25 m (inline_study.md, Astra #3 Part A) |
| B1y inline DM-J4340 yaw | −(+$100) | a cost increase; adopt only after a returnable sample passes (inline_study.md) |
| Pinion v5 → v4 stub + stock keyed pulley | ≈ $15 | the keyed Ø12 is 0.68× (D20) / 1.19× (GIM6010) in rotating-bending fatigue (belts.md, Astra #3 m7) |
| One arm | ≈ $1.3k | fails R2c / R2d (two-handed 20 lb) |
| Base redesign (3-wheel kiwi / hub motors) | ≈ $90–300 | D2: kiwi tip margin 35–46 vs 66–82 mm (A10); no omni-compatible hub motor sourced |
| Two clamp resistors instead of three (robot regen limit 1,663 W) | ≈ $40 | the clamp is the bus's only over-voltage protection; its margin is a safety function |
| JK-B1A8S10P 100 A BMS | ≤ $19 | $76–117 listings vs $95; halves the margin over the 74 A peak |
| DIY 6S2P pack, cheaper DC contactor, a lower contingency | $50–80 each | home-robot safety (unrated welds / contactor), and this pass found +40 % on single lines |
| Sensor pack v2 (encoders, nodes, tactile, ToF) | ≈ $301 | owner D9: sensors over savings (the encoders carry the 0.9 mm accuracy) |
| One PETG bundle | $110 | the print plan needs 17.8 kg with 20 % spare; one bundle needs ≤ 8.3 kg printed |

## Cash view: the M1 kit is not extra

The M1 bench kit's arm and safety-board parts are the robot's (the bench board moves to the robot; the motors, bearings, pinions and hardware of one arm are one of the robot's two). The program's spend is the M1 kit plus the robot BOM less what M1 already bought; only the bench supplies, the stand, the lever, the catch, the coupons and the Step-1 test kit stay on the bench ([M1_BENCH_ARM.md](../M1_BENCH_ARM.md)).

- M1 kit, today's plan, with contingency: $4,447 (Step 1 $2,877 incl. the test kit $1,444, Step 2 $1,570).
- Of it, robot parts (ESTIMATE: every line except the bench-only ones and the test kit): ≈ $2,407 → the robot after M1 needs ≈ $4,306 more, and the program total is ≈ $8,752 (≈ $7,354 if the owner already has the test instruments).
